claims.statement: The Ministry's current list shows 17 legal online betting operators and a state monopoly for online casino and number games.

Polish law requires each online gambling operator to implement a regulator-approved responsible-gambling policy with age verification, registration, activity-control mechanisms, and loss-of-funds controls.
STS currently offers a three-month self-exclusion applied to its own account, evidencing an operator-level workaround rather than national portability.
The European Commission recommendation encourages national self-exclusion registries and operator consultation of them.
GAMSTOP and Sweden's Spelpaus demonstrate multi-operator exclusion checks at registration or login, but both obtain coverage through licensing or statutory requirements.
GDPR consent must be freely given, specific, informed, and withdrawable; profiling or solely automated decisions can add safeguards, so consent-only governance requires specialist analysis.
The foreign comparators imply that regulator-backed coverage, not an optional private consortium, is the critical structural requirement.

contrary_evidence: The reviewed Polish statute specifies operator-level responsible-gambling controls but does not establish the proposed shared registry.
STS already supplies a single-operator self-exclusion, so buyers can claim baseline compliance without a new network.
GAMSTOP and Spelpaus are mandated schemes; they do not validate voluntary Polish operator adoption.
Consent validity, withdrawal, identity matching, joint-controller roles, and automated access denial create unresolved GDPR design questions.
Only 17 licensed betting operators are listed, concentrating revenue and buyer power.

economics.acquisition_route: Secure regulator or association sponsorship before selling operator integrations; successful foreign comparators rely on compulsory licensed-operator participation
economics.founder_net_worth_path: The earlier 10-15 operator scenario is arithmetically possible within the current list of 17 betting operators, but price, mandate, cost, ownership, and adoption are unvalidated; no evidence-backed timing to 5m PLN can be stated
economics.founder_time: About 3 hours/day for product oversight only if gambling counsel, privacy governance, and public-affairs leadership are delegated; coalition formation may not fit that limit
economics.gross_margin_basis: Target 65-80% after high-availability infrastructure, identity matching, legal governance, audits, security, and operator support; unvalidated
economics.payback: Unknown; three paid pilots would not prove a national network unless participation authority and rollout funding are committed
economics.pricing: Unvalidated: 60000-200000 PLN annual operator membership plus implementation and per-check usage; no source disclosed scheme procurement prices or Polish willingness to pay
economics.retention_or_repeat: A mandated login and registration check would be highly recurrent, but Poland currently provides no reviewed mandate for this shared rail

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Mandated operator coverage, accepted governance, identity-matching quality, audited availability, and the default compliance API position
fingerprint.customer: Polish gambling regulator or industry association and licensed online betting operators
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Regulatory and gambling-counsel engagement followed by an association or ministry-sponsored pilot with anchor operators
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Governed self-exclusion registry, minimal yes/no API, audit log, operator onboarding, and compliance reporting; no wagering operation, raw betting-history exchange, or automated addiction score
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Operators or the sponsoring body pay implementation and annual membership fees plus usage for required status checks
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A player requests broad self-exclusion or attempts to register or log in with a participating licensed operator during an active exclusion

founder_fit: Uses data engineering and privacy-preserving system design without operating gambling
A small number of institutional counterparties limits mass-market selling
Measurable compliance and player-protection outcomes suit an analytical founder
Regulatory coalition-building is socially and legally intensive and requires a delegated gambling-policy lead
risks: A private optional network may never achieve useful coverage
Sensitive status leakage could materially harm participants
A false match could wrongly block access and a missed match could defeat exclusion
Operators may resist a control that reduces near-term revenue
Regulator-dependent coalition formation may exceed the founder's preferred social and part-time operating model
A consortium could raise competition and joint-controller concerns if governance is weak

structure.commercial_archetype: Regulated shared utility funded by licensed members
structure.control_point: A regulator-recognized self-exclusion status checked at account registration and login across licensed operators
structure.critical_dependency: A Polish regulator, ministry, or credible operator association must establish a lawful basis, governance mandate, and participation rule; voluntary bilateral consent does not assure coverage

thesis: Provide the technical and governance infrastructure for a player-requested self-exclusion status that participating Polish betting operators check at registration and login. Evidence from Britain and Sweden shows that multi-operator schemes are feasible, but their coverage comes from licensing rules and regulator sponsorship, not optional consent alone. The viable route is therefore a regulator, ministry, or industry-association mandate with an independent data controller, strict minimization, and no exchange of betting history or automated risk score.
title: Regulator-Sponsored Multi-Operator Self-Exclusion Rail
uncertainties: Whether the Polish Ministry, regulator, or an operator association supports a national or sector-wide scheme
Lawful basis and controller allocation for an irrevocable self-exclusion term
Whether self-exclusion status would be treated as health-related special-category data in the proposed context
Operator willingness to fund a system that can reduce play
Identity-match performance for people without stable Polish identifiers
Procurement pricing, integration cost, insurance, audit burden, and founder-net-worth timing
